<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a99e76315210ca4ce682ed3ed2347eadd58d2303` — the merge of head `b36743d69ac312520f08eeb822628036ee86b2b7` into base `706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a99e76315210ca4ce682ed3ed2347eadd58d2303 && git checkout a99e76315210ca4ce682ed3ed2347eadd58d2303
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91 b36743d69ac312520f08eeb822628036ee86b2b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91 && git merge --no-ff b36743d69ac312520f08eeb822628036ee86b2b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 706ac52d570096a47b64283e970bc1a8e569bc91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Not reviewed: .changeset/28727-build-extension-field-suffix.md (prose face; its declaration lines are read under ②).

Inputs: card #28727 (body, claim `6560789923`, os-dev-report `6561648987`); PR #28757 body, file list, `git diff db357f6d..4eb1b664`; the head's 48 check-runs — 37 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failures (`Test Core` ×9, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core` all green).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `os build` narrows** — a stack whose field breaks the `__c` reservation (case (a) `reserved_outside_pair`: a `__c` field on a non-`.custom` package's own object or extension; case (b) `unsuffixed_in_pair`: an unsuffixed `objectExtensions[].fields` key of a `.custom` pair) now exits 1 and writes nothing. **Right.** The call is `findExtensionFieldSuffixRefusals(result.data)` at compile.ts step 3b-iii-bis, the same symbol `validate.ts` calls at 3a-iv over the same parsed `result.data` (both commands parse the lowered stack with `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`); neither the suffix nor the pair rule is spelled in `compile.ts`.
2. **Position** — 3b-iii-bis sits at compile.ts:809–837, directly after the override gate (3b-iii, :778) and ahead of every write: the first `fs.writeFileSync` in the command is the opt-in access-matrix snapshot at 3e (:1004), `cleanupOldRuntimeBundles` is at :1262/:1273, the artifact write at :1292. The output directory is not created before the gate (the new test's `dist/`-absent pin is green in `Test Core`). **Right.**
3. **Faces** — `--json`: this command's envelope `{ success: false, errors, warnings, conversions }` (the override gate's shape, :796), `errors` being the rows validate's `--json` carries (the new test pins deep equality). Text: `printError` heading and `printBulletList` rows string-identical to validate.ts:714–718. **Right**; no second wording.
4. **Package-id reading** — the walk hands each `packages[]` entry under `artifactPackages`' id (`manifest.id`, else `name`, else `packages[N]`) and the bare stack under `manifest.id`; a bare stack with no id is not judged (the judge returns `[]` for a non-string id). This is the walk `validate.ts` already runs, unchanged by the diff, so build ≡ validate on which packages are judged. **Right** (noting the PR body's "a stack naming no id is not judged" holds for the bare stack only; a `packages[]` entry falls back to its name — pre-existing, shared, not a divergence).
5. **Parity ledger** — `findExtensionFieldSuffixRefusals` moves from `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` to `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES`; the ledger is `{}`; the docblock's row history is rewritten (three rows closed). **Right** — the pin `every VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES entry is still validate-only` (:1172) would otherwise red on the compile call, and `both commands run %s` (:929) now holds the build to it.
6. **Public surface** — no export, type, schema, error code or spec key moves; `packages/spec/**` and `packages/metadata-protocol/**` untouched, as the card's claim forbade. `os lint` calls neither this gate nor the override gate on `main`; the parity contract is compile ↔ validate, and this diff leaves lint as it was. **Right; nothing further implied.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28727-build-extension-field-suffix.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, a **BREAKING** banner, exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker (`no-migration-prescription` is in `CATEGORIES` of `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`; `Check Changeset` and the ADR-0087 registration gate are green). The PR body carries the same two line-initial declarations.

- **Level: right.** A non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task §3); `none` takes `patch`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** What a metadata author can write at a metadata door is unchanged — the save, restore, publish, duplicate and install doors and `os validate` already refuse the same fields with the same judge (#28564). The build is a CLI door, not a metadata door; #28643's changeset (`.changeset/28643-build-override-write-gate.md`) declared the identical pair for the identical move.
- **Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` — right.** The build's accept set shrinks; nothing widens.
- **Migration**: the changeset carries the judge's prescription for both cases (rename `x__c`; suffix `region` → `region__c`). No tombstone is owed — no authorable key is removed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` — none to answer.
- Deviation 1 (`origin/main` not merged): verified — `git diff --stat db357f6d..origin/main` (`5493b884`) over the four files and `validate.ts` is empty; PR #28728 (the same parity file) is still open, so the ruling-5 serial merge stays owed by whichever lands second. Not a blocker for this record.
- Deviation 2 (three pushes): a budget note, not a contract matter.
- Deviation 3 (count re-measured): verified — `git grep -nE "[a-z0-9]__c\b"` at `db357f6d` over `examples/**`, `packages/*/src/**`, `skills/**`, tests excluded: 8 hits, all doc comments, 0 field names. **The PR measured case (a) only; I measured case (b):** no `.custom` manifest id exists in `examples/**` or `packages/*/src/**` at the base (`examples/app-showcase` is `com.example.showcase`), so the unsuffixed-in-pair case also narrows on a count of 0.
- `Skills-docs: none`: verified — 0 `__c` hits under `skills/**`; `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` §Object Extension Model names no field spelling and stays true.
- Acceptance note (text face verbatim): verified against validate.ts:712–718 — same heading, same row format, same `noun`/`remedy`.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: ADR-0146 D10 declares the `__c` reservation refused "at publish, at `os validate` and at the install door … so a vendor artifact that ships one is refused on entry". Emitting an artifact every door refuses is not a capability D10 declares to the build's consumer; the parity file's own contract ("`os validate` is the READ-ONLY SUPERSET of the gates `os build` runs") and its #28564 ledger row ("a real gap in the build's direction, reported and not closed") name the pre-diff state as a gap. The diff **makes the spec's own refusal real at the shipping door**, one judge, one walk, no re-spelling; it takes nothing away that any door delivered. Not a consumer-side narrowing of a declared capability.

Attempts to break it:
- *A write before the gate?* None — see ①.2.
- *Build judging a different package set than validate?* Same walk, same `artifactPackages` id rule, same `result.data`; a `.custom` pair's own objects and extensions of them are skipped by the judge at both doors.
- *A false refusal on the tree?* The dogfood battery and `Test Core` are green; both case counts are 0 at base.
- *A face drift?* Text strings identical; `--json` envelope is the command's own, with validate's rows.

**Findings:**
- **should-fix** — `build-extension-field-suffix.test.ts` copies the in-process `run`/`json` helpers verbatim from `build-override-declarations.test.ts` (two copies at head). The parity file's own doctrine is one source per sentence; hoist the helper into `packages/cli/test/helpers/` on the next touch of either file. Not a contract defect; no verdict weight.
- **must-fix** — none.
